text: Never buy a toll road stock without checking this date. Mumbai Pune Expressway, 2030.
IRB and GMR don't own these roads and airports. They hold concessions. The government lends the asset for fixed years, the company runs it and collects tolls or fees, then hands it back.
There are three models. B. O. T., build, operate, transfer. T. O. T., pay upfront to toll an existing road. And hybrid annuity, where the government pays in instalments.
IRB runs twenty eight highway projects, over seventeen thousand lane kilometres, on its own and through two investment trusts.
Its most famous road, the Mumbai Pune Expressway, was won for eight thousand two hundred crore. That contract ends in April 2030.
Others run much longer. The Udaipur highway ends in 2036. Ahmedabad Vadodara, 2043. The Ganga Expressway, 2052. And Hyderabad's Outer Ring Road, 2053.
Now airports. GMR runs Delhi airport on a thirty year term from 2006, which can be extended by thirty more. Hyderabad was extended to 2068. And Goa's Mopa airport has a forty year concession.
Why do end years matter? When a contract ends, that income stops, unless new projects replace it. So watch the years left.
Other risks. Traffic can fall, charges are set by regulators, and debt is often high.
The stocks. IRB trades near nineteen rupees, worth about twenty two thousand crore. GMR Airports, near one hundred, worth about one point zero six lakh crore.
